issues.detail: Covers setup and best practices well but gives little troubleshooting for failure cases such as source maps not resolving, events not arriving, wrong DSN, or set-commits failing without a repository integration.

scenarios.name: nextjs-sentry-setup-secure-sourcemaps
scenarios.rationale: A runs the wizard command the rubric requires and sets `release` in `instrumentation-client.ts`, plus the 0.1 traces rate, replay integration with 0.1/1.0 sample rates, a CI-secret auth token and `withSentryConfig({org, project})`. B never runs the wizard (it uses `npm i @sentry/nextjs`) and omits `release`, though its token handling and CI secret guidance are more thorough.

scenarios.name: python-release-tracking-regression
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric almost exactly: SDK init with the DSN from an env var, environment, release set to the git SHA, and traces_sample_rate 0.1, plus the exact set-commits --auto and deploys commands with --org billing-platform, and a note that a repository integration is required. A has the integration note and mostly correct commands, but it sets release to billing-service@SHA instead of the git SHA, its deploy command omits `--org billing-platform` (it relies on SENTRY_ORG instead), and it adds extra material.

scenarios.name: vite-sourcemaps-and-adblock-noise
scenarios.rationale: Both configure the Sentry Vite plugin last with hidden sourcemaps, an env-based auth token, filesToDeleteAfterUpload, and ignoreErrors for ResizeObserver and extension noise; A adds more extras (allowUrls, beforeSend, a note on already-public maps, a disable guard) while B is more concise and also covers the core, so A is slightly more thorough.
